oewn-00301501-r.learner: used to say that something may be true or may happen, but it is not certain.
examples: Perhaps he thought her too young.
Interested people have perhaps misrepresented each to the other.

oewn-10807146-n.learner: a grown female person, as opposed to a man.
examples: He could not help seeing that you were about five times as pretty as every other woman in the room.
But you know married women have never much time for writing.

oewn-10808492-n.learner: a female person who has an important place in one man's life, as his wife, his mistress, or his girlfriend.
examples: He would not hear a word said against his woman.
He came back from the sea to his woman and his children.

connotation.why: names her by her tie to a particular man

oewn-08494645-n.learner: women taken together as one group.
examples: He liked to make grand speeches about woman and her place in the world.

oewn-00633399-v.learner: to expect something, or to believe it, or to take it to be so.
examples: "Do you suppose them to be in London?"
There are few people in England, I suppose, who have more true enjoyment of music than myself

oewn-00635105-v.learner: to believe something when the grounds for it are unsure or only tried out.
examples: I cannot help supposing that the hope of revenging himself on me was a strong inducement.

oewn-00919271-v.learner: to put something forward as a thing to be taken as true for the moment.
examples: Suppose he arrives late; what shall we do then?

oewn-01009072-v.learner: to get in touch with someone by sending them something in writing.
examples: "Write to me very often, my dear."
Elizabeth wrote the next morning to her mother, to beg that the carriage might be sent for them

oewn-01702148-v.learner: to make a work of literature, such as a book or a poem.
examples: He wrote two novels and a book of poems.
She had written nothing since her first play.

oewn-00995046-v.learner: to tell people something, or show what you feel, by putting it in writing.
examples: In his last pages he wrote about his love for the sea.

oewn-02493222-v.learner: to go and see someone for a short time.
examples: A few days after this visit, Mr. Bingley called again, and alone.
They called at various times of the morning, sometimes separately, sometimes together.

oewn-00794133-v.learner: to tell or ask someone to come to you.
examples: Calling back the servant, therefore, she commissioned him
She called the maid and sent her upstairs.

oewn-01030757-v.learner: to give someone or something a particular name.
examples: They called their second daughter Elizabeth.
The house is called Longbourn.

oewn-02215637-v.learner: to come to have something, whether it is a real thing or not.
examples: I was in great hopes that one of you would have got a husband before you came back.
She got a letter from her aunt that morning.

oewn-00149403-v.learner: to come to be in a certain state or condition.
examples: It got dark before they reached the house.
She was getting tired of waiting.

oewn-00120604-v.learner: to make someone or something move, or to put them in a certain place or state.
examples: He got the children into the carriage before the rain began.
She got her boxes onto the top shelf.

oewn-00101873-r.learner: by a large amount; very much.
examples: The house was far larger than she had expected.
He was far better pleased with the second evening than with the first.

oewn-00102040-r.learner: up to a certain point or amount, and no more.
examples: I had no hesitation in complying with, as far as I thought myself privileged, for you.
She would help her sister, but only so far.

oewn-00101601-r.learner: at, to, or from a place a long way off.
examples: They live far from the village.
He had travelled far to reach the coast.

oewn-10149362-n.learner: a female person who is young.
examples: "You are dancing with the only handsome girl in the room,"
"If you will only tell me what sort of girl Miss King is, I shall know what to think."
The little girl was too small to reach the door handle.
Their first child was a girl.
Mr. Bennet had five girls and no son.
Both of his girls were married before he died.

oewn-00754499-v.learner: to request or demand something from someone.
examples: "What you ask," said Elizabeth, "is no sacrifice on my side"
she did not seem to ask for compassion.

oewn-00899241-v.learner: to put a question to someone and wait for them to answer.
examples: he afterwards took occasion to ask her, when unattended to by any of the rest, whether all her sisters were at Longbourn.

oewn-02634015-v.learner: to need something in order to be useful, fair, or right.
examples: But he had given a reason for his interference, which asked no extraordinary stretch of belief.

oewn-00109919-r.learner: in that place, or at that place.
examples: He stayed there until the rain stopped.
Her gloves were still there on the table.

oewn-00110073-r.learner: to that place, away from the person speaking.
examples: We shall go there in the morning.
Send the boy there with the letter.

oewn-00110206-r.learner: in that matter, or on that point.
examples: You are quite right there, and I will not argue with you.
There I cannot agree with him at all.
